clue.text: Scope yet for develop-isms of adaptable organisms

indicators.note: the coined word develop-isms asks the letters of the two words before it to develop into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A biologist sees plenty of scope for theories of how organisms adapt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop-isms' rearranges SCOPE YET into ECOTYPES; 'for' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecotypes are strains of a species each fitted by natural selection to a particular habitat, so they are organisms that have adapted.

clue.text: Roman conspirator prohibit vermilion?

parts.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators against Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: An odd tale of a Roman plotter banning a shade of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is the mineral mercury sulphide, source of the red pigment, so it is an example of vermilion, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stingy firm

explanation.definitionFit: A miser is called tight-fisted, and a knot held fast is tight.

clue.text: Material of casts, from floppiest arras?

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the two words that follow, rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonders whether plaster casts could be made from very limp tapestries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to rebuild FLOPPIEST ARRAS; the question mark admits that floppy wall hangings are an unlikely source for something rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons set broken limbs in casts of this gypsum plaster, which hardens when wet.

clue.text: Flocked south, having benefited from sunshine

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
being heated by the sun, made warm

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers crowded southwards and enjoyed the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to crowd together in great numbers, as birds do when they flock.

clue.text: Carriage said to be shabby

indicators.note: said tells us the word for shabby is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: mean in the sense of poor, squalid

explanation.surface: Someone's horse-drawn vehicle is rumoured to be run-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a coach but here means a person's bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe deportment, the way a person holds and presents themselves.

clue.text: London's marathon runner seen in St Martin's?

definitions.text: London's marathon runner seen in St Martin's?

parts.words: London's marathon runner seen in St Martin's?
parts.note: not a race entrant but the West End play that has run since 1952, staged at St Martin's Theatre

explanation.surface: A London Marathon competitor is spotted at St Martin's church.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie's play has had the longest run of any in London; 'marathon runner' means long-running show, and St Martin's is the London theatre where it plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's thriller is the world's longest-running stage production, a theatrical marathon.

clue.text: Navigator's instrument, with top broken off, is still working

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a sextant measures the angle of the sun or stars for navigation

explanation.surface: A ship's sextant has lost its top part yet still functions.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, surviving rather than lost.

clue.text: Top job in mail order establishment?

definitions.text: Top job in mail order establishment?

parts.words: Top job in mail order establishment?
parts.note: a senior position at a catalogue firm read instead as the best grade of letter delivery

explanation.surface: Asks about the most senior position in a mail order company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Royal Mail offers first and second-class stamps; a first-class post is also a top-rank appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job, and first-class means top quality; the same phrase names the faster British mail service.

clue.text: Dorabella was in this game, in training

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An opera character took part in this game during practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorabella sounds like Mozart's opera, but it is the title of Elgar's tenth Enigma Variation, a portrait of Dora Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Enigma Variations contain a movement called Dorabella, so she appears in that work.

clue.text: Below the line, the exact number to quail, possibly

definitions.text: Below the line, the exact number

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters before it may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A stray instruction about counting quail, put in a footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below the line' points to the denominator of a fraction: an aliquot part is a divisor that goes into a number exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic an aliquot part divides a whole with no remainder, like 3 into 12.

clue.text: Friday's Figaro?

parts.note: Robinson Crusoe's servant Man Friday and Rossini's barber, who sings that he does every job in town

explanation.surface: Asks who Figaro was on a Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Man Friday' is a general helper, and Figaro in The Barber of Seville calls himself the town's do-it-all in the aria 'Largo al ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant who handles every kind of chore is a jack of all trades, the role of both Friday and Figaro.

clue.text: Getting and believing in the saw?

definitions.text: Getting and believing in the saw?

parts.words: Getting and believing in the saw?
parts.note: the saw is a proverb, and the old saying links perceiving with believing; getting also means understanding

explanation.surface: Asks about understanding and trusting a woodworking tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool, but means a saying: the proverb pairs this word with 'is believing'; 'Getting' in the sense 'I see' is the other half.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a point is to understand it, as in 'I see'; the proverb says perception leads to belief.

clue.text: Large scale manufacturer spur comrades in such a way?

indicators.note: asks whether the factory treats the letters of the two words before as material to reprocess into a new order

explanation.surface: A big factory urges its fellow workers on in this fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in such a way?' rearranges SPUR COMRADES; the surface hints at factory productivity drives.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm turning out standardised goods in huge quantities on assembly lines works on a large scale.

clue.text: Traditional airs heard in fireworks displays

definitions.meaning: the large framework fireworks fixed in place at a display

explanation.definitionFit: A set piece is a fixed, prescribed composition in music, and a mounted framework of fireworks lit at a show.

clue.text: Properly delivered, from good stock

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase describes a smooth birth; as an idiom it means of aristocratic descent.

clue.text: Sticky confections for kids

parts.note: fruit on a stick coated in hardened caramel, sold at fairs and on Bonfire Night

explanation.surface: Describes gooey sweets made for children.
explanation.walkthrough: These are a fairground and Bonfire Night (5 November, Britain's fireworks night) treat; 'sticky' also refers to the stick they are held by.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel-coated fruit is a sweet treat, messy to eat and mounted on a stick.

clue.text: A torque twisted in the Circle Line?

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of the words before are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning force bent out of shape on the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Tube route; here it is a circle drawn round the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circle of latitude midway between the poles is a line circling the Earth.

clue.text: Head's first quarrel in school

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Head's

parts.note: a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of short arrow

explanation.surface: A headteacher's first row at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like an argument but means a bolt. Harrow is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow School is a well-known boys' boarding school in north-west London.

clue.text: Layer of beast in its back

indicators.note: the word for beast is read from its back end, so written backwards

explanation.surface: A layer found in an animal's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin plate or sheet, one stratum of a material.

clue.text: No tulips turn out perfect

indicators.note: turn out signals the letters of the words before are turned into another form

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that no tulips come up flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoilt is undamaged and intact, in flawless condition.

clue.text: School governor with one eye?

parts.note: a school board member reads instead as something controlling a pupil, the centre of the eye

explanation.surface: Asks about a one-eyed member of a school's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' leads to pupils, and the pupil is part of the eye; the optic nerve or eye itself governs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic means relating to the eye or sight, and is also a name for the eye itself.

clue.text: Voucher for one penny in Crete, when travelling

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the rearranged island
travelling moves the letters of the island's name around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ticket for a single penny when touring Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when travelling' rearranges CRETE into RECET, and 'in' puts I and P inside it, giving RECE-IP-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written slip acknowledging payment, proof of purchase like a voucher.

clue.text: Love to point out preference

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: out tells us the letters of point are put out of order

explanation.surface: Advice to show affection to point out what you prefer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as zero is a tennis score; the round figure stands for the letter O at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice, the thing one opts for or prefers.

clue.text: Allows snow to drift

indicators.note: drifting moves things about, so the letters of snow shift position

explanation.surface: Someone permits the snow to pile into drifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allows' is in the sense of admitting or acknowledging something.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to admit or concede it, an old sense of granting.

clue.text: Mum puts it back in modern housing

indicators.note: the modern word houses the turned word inside it
back means the word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: Mother puts it back on the shelf in her new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the adjective for silent. 'back' turns IT into TI and 'housing' puts it in RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means staying silent, and a reserved, tight-lipped person says little.
